articles.title: Rochdale to Hold Memorial for Comedian Jimmy Cricket Ahead of Funeral
articles.excerpt: Rochdale will pay tribute to beloved comedian Jimmy Cricket, who passed away on August 3, with a lying in state at St Patrick’s Church and a funeral at Salford Cathedral.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale will have the opportunity to remember legendary comedian Jimmy Cricket, who died on August 3 at the age of 80, following a short illness. Known for his clean humour and catchphrase 'And there’s more', Cricket became a household name in the 1970s and was a prominent supporter of local charities and causes.

His body will lie in state at St Patrick’s Catholic Church on Watts Street in Rochdale on Thursday, August 20, from 3pm to 5pm. This will allow fans and friends to pay their respects before his life is celebrated at Salford Cathedral later that evening. A vigil mass for the reception of his body will begin at 7pm.

The funeral service will take place at Salford Cathedral on Friday, August 21, at 1.30pm. Mourners are encouraged to wear bow ties, which, along with his iconic Wellington boots, became synonymous with Cricket's persona. His contributions to local charities and the joy he brought to audiences will be celebrated during the memorial events.

Jimmy Cricket's legacy as a beloved entertainer and community figure will be remembered fondly by many in Rochdale, where he made his home. His passing marks the end of an era for those who appreciated his unique brand of comedy and his commitment to supporting local initiatives.

articles.title: Plans Submitted for 350 New Homes in Bamford, Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Developers are moving forward with plans to build hundreds of homes on former green belt land in Bamford, following the removal of its protected status in 2024.
articles.content_html:
Developers Northstone have submitted a hybrid planning application for 350 new homes on former green belt land in Bamford, Rochdale. The proposed development is set to transform a significant area of grassland located off Norden Road, which has been earmarked for housing following the adoption of the Greater Manchester-wide Places for Everyone plan in 2024.

The plans come as part of a broader initiative to address housing demand in the region, with the Bamford suburb anticipating the construction of 450 houses in total. The area has seen increasing interest from developers since the land was removed from green belt status, allowing for potential residential development.

The application will be split across two sites on the western edge of the designated land. Northstone is a subsidiary of The Peel Group, a major landowner and developer in the region, indicating a significant investment in local housing infrastructure.

Next steps will involve the planning authority reviewing the application, with local residents likely to be informed about the development process and any public consultations that may arise. This project could have implications for local services and infrastructure as the area prepares for an influx of new residents.

articles.title: NHS Staff at Rochdale Infirmary to Strike Over Overtime Pay Dispute
articles.excerpt: More than 350 staff at Rochdale Infirmary and three other Greater Manchester hospitals will strike for three days next week due to a dispute over overtime payments, according to UNISON.
articles.content_html:
More than 350 employees of the Northern Care Alliance Foundation Trust (NCA), including nurses and clinical support workers at Rochdale Infirmary, will strike for three days next week. The strike is scheduled for Monday 24th, Wednesday 26th, and Friday 28th August, as part of an ongoing dispute regarding overtime payments.

The dispute arises from the NCA's use of NHS Professionals (NHSP) to manage overtime, which has reportedly led to staff earning less than their usual pay rates. UNISON claims that some staff are missing out on more than £80 per shift due to this arrangement, which contradicts their contractual entitlements to time-and-a-half pay when covering staff shortages.

Kevin Dolan, UNISON's North West regional organiser, expressed frustration over the situation, stating that a resolution offer was made by NCA management but subsequently withdrawn before discussions could take place. He emphasised that staff are simply asking for what they are contractually owed and accused NCA leadership of lacking commitment to resolving the issue.

In addition to the strikes, staff from all four affected hospitals, including Rochdale Infirmary, Royal Oldham Hospital, Fairfield Hospital in Bury, and Salford Royal Hospital, will gather in Salford on Wednesday 26th August for a unified day of protest.

articles.title: Lift Out of Service at Derker Tram Stop
articles.excerpt: The lift at Derker tram stop is currently out of service, affecting access for passengers. Step-free access is available via alternative routes until further notice.
articles.content_html:
The lift at Derker tram stop has been out of service since 8:09pm on 18 August 2026, impacting passengers using the tram service. There is currently no confirmed date for when the lift will be restored.

For customers travelling towards Manchester, step-free access is available via a ramp from Cromford Street directly to the Manchester-bound platform. Passengers heading towards Rochdale can also use a ramp from Cromford Street, followed by a track crossing to access the Rochdale-bound platform.

Transport for Greater Manchester has apologised for any inconvenience caused by this disruption and is advising passengers to plan their journeys accordingly. Passengers are encouraged to check the latest travel alerts on the Transport for Greater Manchester website for ongoing updates regarding the lift's status and any other travel disruptions.

Further information can be found on the Transport for Greater Manchester website, where live travel alerts are regularly updated.
